Çentik - Turns the MacBook notch into a live island for music, system stats, an AI chat with your own Claude, Gemini or Ollama, clipboard history, a file shelf and meeting alerts.

summary.one_liner: Çentik is a free, open-source macOS app that turns the MacBook notch into an interactive island for music, system stats, AI chat, clipboard history, a file shelf and meeting alerts.
keywords: see cpu usage from the notch
chat with local model on mac
summary.what_it_does: Çentik places a panel in the area of the MacBook notch that shows music from Spotify and Apple Music with artwork and playback controls. It displays live CPU, memory, GPU, network, disk and per-app usage with graphs, and lets you pin two metrics to the sides of the notch. It offers an AI chat that connects to your installed Claude Code or Gemini CLI, a Claude or Gemini API key stored in the Keychain, or a local Ollama model; the chat is text-only and cannot read files or run commands. It keeps a clipboard history, a shelf where files can be dropped and dragged out, and a notes and to-do list saved on disk. It also shows volume, brightness, battery and network indicators, alerts for coding-agent events, meeting countdowns with Join buttons, screenshot and download previews, a timer, a mirror, weather from Open-Meteo, and a keep-awake option.
use_cases: see system stats at a glance on a MacBook
control Spotify or Apple Music from the notch
chat with Claude, Gemini or a local Ollama model from the menu bar
keep a clipboard history on macOS
park files temporarily and drag them out
get countdown alerts before meetings and join with one click
get notified when Claude Code needs approval
how_to_run: Or download Centik.dmg from the latest release and drag Çentik to Applications
If macOS blocks the first launch, allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security, or run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Çentik.app
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd Centik, ./build.sh --install
Hover over the notch or press ⌃⌥N to open
notable: Notch-native UI with five themes (Night, Aurora, Glass, Neon, Minimal) and an accent that follows album art
Bring-your-own AI: uses existing Claude Code or Gemini CLI sign-in, API keys in Keychain, or fully local Ollama
Privacy-focused: no account, analytics or crash reporting; clipboard items from password managers are never stored
Scriptable via distributed notifications and a hook script that lets other tools raise alerts
English and Turkish interface; works on Macs without a notch too
caveats: The app is not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS blocks the first launch and requires a manual override
Browser media playback (e.g., YouTube) is not shown; Now Playing data is unavailable since macOS 15.4, so only Spotify and Apple Music are supported
Brightness uses the private DisplayServices framework and turns off on unsupported displays; the system's own volume and brightness HUDs still appear
